statement: The resolver fails open: `$request->route('workspace')` is only a `Workspace` instance when the route action type-hints it (implicit binding), so any future route added to the `/w/{workspace}` group whose controller lacks a `Workspace $workspace` parameter silently returns `null`, skipping both the 403 membership check and tenant activation, and serving every tenant's rows unscoped.

The membership gate accepts only `wsp_workspace_user` rows with `status='active'` and ignores `wsp_workspaces.owner_id`, yet no production code path (no Action, seeder, observer or factory) ever writes a pivot row, so a workspace owner is 403'd out of their own workspace and the route is reachable only for hand-seeded data.

The proof route is a Closure shipped in production `routes/web.php`, which makes `php artisan route:cache` / `optimize` throw `LogicException: Unable to prepare route [w/{workspace}] for serialization. Uses Closure.`, breaking the standard production deploy step.

`abort_unless(...)` puts an HTTP-guard inside a non-HTTP tenancy class, violating `.ai/guidelines/architecture.md` ("Запрещено в `*Service`: HTTP-guard (`abort_*`) ... это Form Request, Policy, контроллер"), and overloads the `resolve(): ?Tenant` contract so callers cannot distinguish "no tenant" from "forbidden".

Nothing verifies the actual claim of the change end-to-end: the isolation test bypasses HTTP and sets the tenant by hand via `app(TenantService::class)->setCurrent()`, while the only route under test returns just the slug and queries no `TenantModel`, so the middleware → resolver → service → `TenantScope` chain is never exercised over a request.
Returning 403 for an existing workspace while an unknown slug yields 404 gives any authenticated user a workspace-slug enumeration oracle; 404 for both cases would not leak existence.

The resolver hardcodes the table name `'wsp_workspaces.id'` (duplicating `Workspace::$table` instead of `$workspace->getQualifiedKeyName()`) and the magic string `'active'`, which together with `'member'`/`'invited'` in the tests and the migration defaults spreads an untyped membership vocabulary across four files despite the project's `enum-attributes` convention.

The new workspace group introduces a second, ad-hoc authorization mechanism (membership check buried in a tenancy resolver) alongside the `azguard.panel:app` + `check.access` stack that every sibling protected group in the same file uses, so access rules for workspace pages will diverge from the rest of the app.

The commit message and `config/corex.php` both assert "вне workspace-группы скоуп снят", but no test hits a `TenantModel` outside `/w/{workspace}` to confirm the scope is actually inert there after the switch from `NullTenantService` to `ContainerTenantService`.
`expect(Project::query()->count())->toBe(1)` only counts rows and would pass if the scope filtered to the *wrong* workspace; the test never asserts the surviving record's identity or `workspace_id`.
Activating `ContainerTenantService` also switches on `BelongsToTenant`'s auto-stamping of `workspace_id` on create, but no test covers the write path — only reads are asserted.

Replacing the stateless `NullTenantService` with a stateful container singleton introduces per-process tenant state that `ResolveTenant` never clears (no `forget()`), and no test pins that the tenant does not survive across requests or queued jobs in long-lived runtimes.
The `memberOf()` helper is declared as a global function inside a Pest test file rather than in `tests/Pest.php`, so a same-named helper in any other test file will fatal with a redeclaration error.

`getRouteKeyName()` is documented with a `//` line comment while every other method in the file (and in `User::workspaces()` added by the same commit) uses a docblock, breaking the file's own documentation style.

`ResolveTenant` is a route-level middleware that runs *after* the `web` group's `SubstituteBindings`, so any tenant-owned model bound implicitly in a nested route (Фаза 5 migration of product pages, e.g. `/w/{a}/documents/{id}`) is resolved before the tenant is active and therefore escapes `TenantScope`, allowing cross-workspace access.

The resolver fails open — a missing/unbound `{workspace}` param or an unauthenticated request returns `null`, and CoreX's `ResolveTenant` treats `null` as "no tenant" and continues, so the request runs fully unscoped instead of being denied (today masked only by the enclosing `['auth','verified']` group, which the resolver itself does not require).

Switching `TenantService` to the container-singleton `ContainerTenantService` introduces per-process mutable tenant state that is never `forget()`-ed at end of request, so on any reused worker (Octane, as the architecture doc's "Octane-ready дисциплина" targets, or long-lived processes) a stale tenant leaks into the next request and silently scopes it to the wrong workspace.

Access control (membership → 403) is implemented inside a tenant resolver via `abort_unless`, violating the project's `project-map` rule "проверка прав — Policy + permissions enum" and CLAUDE.md's ban on HTTP-guards outside the HTTP layer, and breaking the `TenantResolver` contract whose documented semantics are "return null when unresolved" (a console/queue caller now gets an `HttpException`).

The central claim of the commit — that `TenantModel` queries auto-scope *inside* `/w/{workspace}` — is never tested end-to-end: the isolation test bypasses HTTP and sets the tenant by hand via `app(TenantService::class)->setCurrent()`, while the HTTP test only asserts the echoed slug, so the middleware→service→scope wiring is unverified.

Only pivot `status` is checked; the workspace's own `plan_status` column (schema default `active`, i.e. the field modelling suspension) is ignored, so a suspended/deactivated workspace remains fully accessible to its members.
Non-members receive 403 for an existing slug but 404 for a non-existent one, turning `/w/{slug}` into a workspace-existence enumeration oracle for any authenticated user.

Tenant context is established only on the HTTP boundary, so queued jobs, events and console commands dispatched from inside `/w/{workspace}` run with no active tenant — reads are silently unscoped and `BelongsToTenant`'s create-stamp leaves `workspace_id` unset — and neither the code nor the config comment acknowledges this limitation.

`getRouteKeyName()` is overridden globally on the model to serve a single route, changing implicit binding and `route()` URL generation for every present and future `{workspace}` parameter, where the localized idiom `prefix('w/{workspace:slug}')` would have confined the change to this group.

A proof-of-concept closure route is shipped into production `routes/web.php`, permanently exposing a JSON debug endpoint at `/w/{slug}` and making the route file non-serializable for `php artisan route:cache`.

The change introduces a new top-level layer `app/Tenancy/` and flips a core architectural switch (multi-tenancy on), but no documentation or agent context is updated — `docs/03_Dev/Architecture_FlexCRM.md`, `.ai/guidelines/*` and the `project-map` directory map are untouched, contrary to CLAUDE.md and the `cross-layer-change-checklist` step 6.
The resolver's two `return null` branches (unauthenticated request, non-`Workspace` route parameter) have zero coverage, so the fail-open path — the security-critical one — is entirely unverified.

The explicit claim in the config comment and commit message that "вне workspace-группы скоуп снят" (existing non-`/w/` pages keep working unscoped) has no regression test, despite being the guarantee that this change is backward-compatible for all product pages not yet migrated.

Activating `ContainerTenantService` also activates `BelongsToTenant`'s create-time auto-stamping of `workspace_id`, but only read isolation is tested — no test asserts that a `TenantModel` created under an active tenant is stamped with the right workspace.

The global helper `memberOf()` is declared inside a test file instead of `tests/Pest.php`, where the project keeps its global test helpers (`userWithMemberRole`), risking a fatal redeclaration as soon as another tenancy test file needs the same helper.

The membership status literal `'active'` (and `'member'` in the test) is hardcoded and duplicated across resolver and test rather than expressed as a backed enum in `app/Enums/`, which `project-map` designates as the home for "статусы, роли, типы".

`User::workspaces()` exposes all memberships regardless of pivot status, so every consumer must independently remember `wherePivot('status', 'active')`; no `activeWorkspaces()` relation or pivot scope encapsulates the rule that the resolver depends on.

The query hardcodes the string `'wsp_workspaces.id'`, duplicating `Workspace::$table` instead of using `whereKey()`/`$workspace->getQualifiedKeyName()`, so a table rename silently breaks the membership check rather than failing at compile time.

The proof route is defined as a closure, the only closure route in the whole routes tree, so `php artisan route:cache` / `artisan optimize` in a production deploy now fails with "Unable to prepare route [w/{workspace}] for serialization. Uses Closure."

`ResolveTenant` is attached as route-level middleware and therefore runs after the `web` group's `SubstituteBindings`, so any nested tenant-owned model bound implicitly under `/w/{workspace}` (e.g. the Phase-5 `/w/{workspace}/projects/{project}`) is resolved with no active tenant and thus unscoped, contradicting the group comment's guarantee that "TenantModel-модели авто-скоупятся".
A temporary proof/debug endpoint returning raw internal JSON is merged into the production route file with only a prose comment and no TODO/ticket marker tying it to its removal in Phase 5.

The resolver fails open on unexpected input — a missing route parameter or a null user returns `null`, which `ResolveTenant` translates into "no tenant" (scope silently disabled) rather than a denial, so if the group is ever used outside the `auth` middleware the request runs unscoped instead of 403.

Non-member access to an existing workspace returns 403 while an unknown slug returns 404, letting any authenticated user enumerate which workspace slugs (derived from customer company names) exist in the installation.

The resolver conflates tenant resolution with authorization by calling `abort_unless` inside a `TenantResolver` contract documented to merely "determine the active tenant" and return `?Tenant`, so any non-HTTP caller of `resolve()` receives an HttpException instead of a null result.

`$request->user()` is typed as `Illuminate\Contracts\Auth\Authenticatable`, which does not declare `workspaces()`, so the membership check relies on an undeclared method with no `instanceof User` narrowing and would fatal for any other user provider.

The membership query hardcodes the table literal `wsp_workspaces.id` and forces a join to the workspaces table, duplicating schema knowledge the model already owns when `wherePivot('workspace_id', $workspace->getKey())` would suffice.

Membership status is compared against the bare magic string `'active'`, duplicated across the migration default, the resolver and the test helper, with no enum or shared constant despite the project's enum-attributes convention.

`User::workspaces()` re-declares the same pivot configuration (`withPivot(['role','status'])->withTimestamps()`) already present in `Workspace::users()` and neither side binds the existing `WorkspaceUser` model via `->using()`, giving three independent representations of one pivot that can drift.

`getRouteKeyName()` changes route-key resolution and `route()` URL generation for `Workspace` application-wide (including any future Filament resource) while the justifying comment scopes the decision to a single route, and a mutable slug would silently break every previously issued URL with no redirect path.

`TenantService` is registered as a container singleton in CoreServiceProvider, and switching it to the now-stateful `ContainerTenantService` introduces mutable per-request state that nothing ever clears (`forget()` is never called), so the active tenant leaks across requests under any long-lived runtime such as Octane or Reverb.

Tenancy is activated only on the HTTP path via route middleware, so console commands, scheduled tasks and queue workers never set a tenant and every `TenantModel` read in those lanes still returns rows from all workspaces, with no guard or assertion covering that gap.

The test named "активирует тенант внутри /w/{workspace}" asserts only HTTP 200 and the echoed slug, both of which the closure produces from route-model binding alone, so it would still pass with `ResolveTenant` and the resolver removed entirely — the commit's headline behavior has no failing-on-regression test.

The isolation test proves scoping only after calling `app(TenantService::class)->setCurrent()` by hand, bypassing routing, middleware and the resolver, so no test connects the HTTP path to actual `TenantModel` scoping and the end-to-end multi-tenancy claim is unverified.
No test covers the write path that this commit newly activates — `BelongsToTenant::creating` auto-stamping `workspace_id` from the active tenant is exercised nowhere.
The config comment's claim "Вне workspace-группы (или без активного тенанта) скоуп снят" is asserted by no test, leaving the unscoped-outside-the-group behavior undocumented by evidence.

The `memberOf()` helper is declared as a global function inside a Pest test file rather than in `tests/Pest.php` or a dedicated helpers file, so a second declaration of that name anywhere in the suite becomes a fatal redeclaration error.

`check_target=True` by default silently turns a previously-succeeding write into an uncaught `OSError` for all ~103 existing `atomic_write_text`/`atomic_write_json` call sites across skiller/harness/maind/analyst, with no caller inventory proving none of them legitimately targets a symlink (e.g. a dotfiles-managed `.claude/settings.json` written by `skiller connect`, while the repo itself ships `skills-ssot/snippets/symlink-sync.sh` that symlinks managed files).

The `st_nlink != 1` refusal is fail-closed on ordinary regular files that merely happen to be hardlinked (`cp -al`, hardlink-dedup backups, package-manager stores) where `os.replace` is safe and non-destructive, and since no call site passes `check_target=False` such a path becomes permanently unwritable through core with no reachable opt-out.

The helper raises a bare `OSError` with no `errno` instead of the repo's `core.term.die` refusal convention, so a safety refusal is indistinguishable from a real I/O error for any caller with an `except OSError` fallback and surfaces to CLI users as an unhandled traceback rather than the promised named reason.

The docstring claims "Один `lstat`" but the body performs three stat syscalls (`os.lstat` + `os.path.islink` + `os.path.isfile`, the last of which resolves symlinks) instead of deriving both predicates from the single `st.st_mode` via `stat.S_ISLNK`/`S_ISREG`.

The check-then-`os.replace` sequence leaves a residual TOCTOU window in which the target can be swapped for a symlink after the check passes, and neither docstring states the guard is best-effort rather than an enforceable invariant.

Because the refusal fires inside `atomic_write_text` after callers have already run their own pre-write side effects, `skiller connect` leaves a stray `<dest>.bak` and prints "Бэкап: …" immediately before the write aborts, producing misleading output plus an orphan artifact.

The entry is filed under `### Added` although it changes the default runtime behavior of two pre-existing public functions (`atomic_write_text`/`atomic_write_json`) from "write succeeds" to "raises" — a `Changed`/breaking-behavior note per release-discipline, and the claim "поведение байт-в-байт прежнее" only holds for the two target classes it enumerates.

The new public helper `assert_safe_replace_target` is not re-exported in `core/__init__.py` nor listed in `__all__`, breaking the monorepo's documented `from core import ...` public-API convention — visible in the new test, which must import `from core.io import ...` unlike `test_core.py`.

The docstring's inventory of manual duplicates in `packages/maind/lib/maind/provider_deploy.py` names four functions but omits `_d108_unchanged_mcp_artifact` (line 258), so the named roadmap follow-up would silently skip a duplicate site.

The invariant now exists in two divergent definitions — core rejects symlink + non-regular + hardlink, while the six untouched `provider_deploy.py` copies reject only symlink/non-regular — so this commit deepens the duplication it documents instead of leaving one semantics.

`check_target=False` ships with zero call sites anywhere in the repo, i.e. a speculative escape hatch added without a demonstrated legitimate consumer, contrary to the repo's "фичу внедряем по факту измеренной проблемы" framing.
The "не регулярный файл" refusal branch (FIFO/socket/device/directory) has no test at all, despite being one of the three refusal reasons and despite the module docstring advertising "4 класса цели".
No test exercises `atomic_write_json(..., check_target=...)`, so a regression that drops the new kwarg forwarding to `atomic_write_text` would go undetected.
Only the symlink refusal is verified end-to-end through `atomic_write_text`; the hardlink refusal path is never checked for tmp cleanup and target-content preservation.

No regression evidence covers the ~103 pre-existing production call sites against the new default — the claim that only "несуществующая цель и обычный файл" matter is asserted, not measured against any caller.

Хардening неполон: сам `<name>.tmp` не проверяется, и `tmp.write_text`/`os.chmod` пройдут по заранее подложенной symlink-цели `<name>.tmp`, оставляя ровно тот symlink-write, который коммит декларирует закрытым (включая запись файлов с `mode=0o600`).

Проверка включена по умолчанию для ~120 call-site'ов, пишущих ВНЕ дерева репо (`maind/health.py:212` — `CLAUDE.md`, `health.py:286,345` — `.claude/settings.json`, `mcpconfig.py:76` — `.mcp.json`), где symlink-конфиги от dotfile-менеджеров и hardlink'и штатны; ни один вызов не ловит `OSError`, поэтому пользователь получит голый traceback вместо `die()`-сообщения, а оценка «риск регресса нулевой» в ТЗ смотрела только на дерево репо.

Нарушено явное Implementation Rule P8.7 «один `lstat` цели» и повторяющий его докстринг «Один `lstat`»: фактически делается три stat-syscall'а (`os.lstat` + `os.path.islink` → lstat + `os.path.isfile` → stat) вместо разбора уже полученного `st.st_mode` через `stat.S_ISLNK`/`S_ISREG`.

Из-за повторных stat'ов решение принимается по трём разным снимкам ФС: если цель исчезнет между `os.lstat` и `os.path.isfile`, вызов отказывает с «не регулярный файл», хотя контракт (и ТЗ «байт-в-байт прежнее поведение») требует для несуществующей цели молча вернуться.

Классический TOCTOU: между `assert_safe_replace_target(path)` и `os.replace(tmp, path)` цель можно подменить на symlink (нет `O_NOFOLLOW`/dirfd-привязки), то есть инвариант защищает от случайного symlink'а, но не от активного атакующего — и ни докстринг, ни CHANGELOG этой границы не оговаривают.

`assert_safe_replace_target` не реэкспортирован в фасаде `core/__init__.py` (`from .io import …` / `__all__`), в отличие от всех прочих публичных примитивов `core.io`, — будущий перевод `maind/provider_deploy.py` (который импортирует `from core import atomic_write_text`) будет вынужден лезть в `core.io` в обход конвенции пакета.
Ветка «не регулярный файл» (`core/io.py:121-122`) — одна из трёх задекларированных причин отказа — не покрыта ни одним тестом (нет кейса FIFO/сокета/каталога), хотя `os.mkfifo` доступен в stdlib.
Новый публичный параметр `atomic_write_json(..., check_target=...)` и его проброс (`core/io.py:166`) не покрыты ни одним тестом — проверяется только `atomic_write_text`.

Ассерт `assertIn("ссылка", …)` не различает ветки: подстрока входит и в сообщение про жёсткую ссылку («жёсткая ссылка»), поэтому тест пройдёт и при неверной классификации цели — нужна подстрока «символьная».
Отказ по hardlink проверен только на уровне хелпера — интеграции «`atomic_write_text` по hardlink-цели отказывает и подчищает `.tmp`» (и кейса битого/висячего symlink'а) в тестах нет.

Утверждение «Несуществующая цель и обычный файл — поведение байт-в-байт прежнее» неточно: обычный регулярный файл с `st_nlink > 1` теперь отвергается, то есть для части «обычных файлов» поведение как раз изменилось.

Инвентарь дублей в докстринге неполон: пятая ручная копия того же инварианта — `_d108_unchanged_mcp_artifact` (`packages/maind/lib/maind/provider_deploy.py:258`, инвертированная форма `path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink()`) — не названа, хотя ТЗ требовало полный список по грепу `is_symlink`.

Обязательная Validation #2 item'а (регресс всех пакетов зелёный) сейчас невоспроизводима: `bash packages/maind/scripts/test.sh` даёт `FAILED (failures=2)` (`test_provider_deploy`, `test_p13_cross_project_memory_docs`) — падения к `core/io.py` не относятся, но заявленное свидетельство «все зелёные» подтвердить нельзя (core: 244 OK, skiller: 491 OK, task validate OK, ruff чист).
Перехватывается только `FileNotFoundError`: `NotADirectoryError` (компонент пути — файл) и `PermissionError` уходят наружу как сырые `OSError` без обязательной по ТЗ формулировки «путь + причина».

The `check_target=False` escape hatch is documented as the exit for a package that "легально пишет через symlink-цель", but `os.replace` renames onto the link itself, so the flag silently destroys the symlink and leaves the real file stale — the documented use case is unachievable with this flag (verified: after `atomic_write_text(link, "new", check_target=False)` the link is a regular file and the target keeps its old content).

`assert_safe_replace_target` is not re-exported from `core/__init__.py` (nor listed in `__all__`) while every other public `core.io` symbol is, so the declared dedup consumers in `packages/maind/lib/maind/provider_deploy.py` cannot import it via the repo-wide `from core import ...` convention.

Rejecting any regular file with `st_nlink != 1` turns previously-succeeding writes into hard failures on hardlink-deduplicated trees (rsync `--link-dest`, backup/CoW copies), and `check_target` is all-or-nothing so a caller cannot keep the symlink guard while tolerating hardlinks (verified: `atomic_write_text` on a hardlinked target now raises `st_nlink=2`).

The no-regression evidence behind D49 ("отслеживаемых симлинков в дереве нет") was gathered from `git ls-files` of the monorepo only, while nearly all real call sites write outside the repo — `~/.claude/settings.json` (skiller/connect.py:201), project `CLAUDE.md` (maind/health.py:212), `~/.swissknifeman` config, Brain vault scripts (skiller/brain_sync.py:94) — where dotfile-manager/vault symlinks are common and no test or scan covers them.

The "не регулярный файл" raise branch (FIFO/socket/directory) ships with no test although the module docstring claims "4 класса цели" coverage; the four tests cover missing/regular/symlink/hardlink only, leaving a distinct new failure path unguarded against regression.

The helper raises bare `OSError` with a prose message (no errno, no dedicated exception class) and no call site wraps it, so a user with a symlinked target gets a raw Python traceback instead of the repo's `die()` diagnostic convention, and typed-error callers such as maind's `ProviderDeployError` taxonomy would have to string-match to reclassify it.

The docstring claims "Один `lstat`, обход/резолв цепочки симлинков … НЕ производятся", but the body issues three stat syscalls and `os.path.isfile` does follow symlinks; `st_nlink` is read from the first `lstat` while `islink`/`isfile` re-stat, so a path replaced mid-check yields a mixed view of two inodes.

The check is TOCTOU-racy with respect to the following `os.replace` — a symlink planted in the window between the assert and the rename is still clobbered — yet the `assert_safe` name and the CHANGELOG "инвариант" framing present it as a guarantee rather than an advisory accident-guard.

The entry reassures that "несуществующая цель и обычный файл — поведение байт-в-байт прежнее" while the same entry rejects hardlinks, and a hardlinked regular file is an "обычный файл" whose behavior changed from success to `OSError` — the reassurance contradicts the change it documents.

The new `check_target` keyword on `atomic_write_json` and its passthrough to `atomic_write_text` have no test at all; every new-invariant test exercises `atomic_write_text` directly, so a broken forward of the kwarg would pass the suite.

The target check runs after `tmp.write_text` and `os.chmod`, so the entire payload is written to disk and then discarded on refusal; asserting before the tmp write would be cheaper and would shrink the check→replace window.

The root CLAUDE.md description of the shared primitive (`core.io` — «атомарная запись tmp+`os.replace`») was not updated with the new target invariant or the `check_target` parameter, so the monorepo-level description of a cross-package primitive now understates its contract.

A legacy or custom `config.json` that has a working `check_command` but no `checks[]` array is reported as `unconfigured (no-op)` even though `review-gate.sh:78-89` will execute it — verified empirically — which is precisely the "looks off but silently runs" inversion this item claims to eliminate, and precisely the population created by the new migration guard that refuses to touch non-stub configs.

Doctor prints the *declared* per-check mode (`configured: G1, G2 (strict), W1 (warn)`) and never applies the global `MODE=warn` downgrade from `run-checks.sh:64`, so on the shipped default `env.ini` (`MODE=warn`) doctor advertises two strict checks that can never block.

The shipped `env.ini` default is `MODE=warn` and `intended_strict` requires `MODE != warn`, so the shipped `"mode": "strict"` declarations for `generated-assets`/`plan-lint` are inert on every default install — the feature ships as a warn-only advisory despite CHANGELOG/CLAUDE.md presenting strict enforcement.

`git diff --name-only` emits repo-root-relative paths while `git ls-files --others` emits cwd-relative paths (verified in a scratch repo), and `[ -f "$f" ]` resolves against the hook's `cwd`, so whenever the SubagentStop payload `cwd` is a subdirectory of the repo every tracked-modified generated file fails the existence test and the check silently returns clean.

All three checks inspect the entire working tree (unstaged + staged + untracked) rather than the diff the just-finished subagent produced, so any pre-existing dirt — including work in flight from before the session — is attributed to that subagent and re-blocks it on every stop; the same defect applies at `plan-lint.sh:8` and `tests-touched.sh:8`.

The migration criterion is a hard-coded sha256 with no in-repo source file, no fixture and no test (the old `config.json` was gitignored and never tracked), and the constant `2ba2ef65…` does not correspond to the byte string `{"version":1,"check_command":""}` stated in the adjacent comment, the README and the CHANGELOG (that compact form hashes to `9c5c7350…`), so nobody can re-derive or falsify the guard.

The three tests exercise only `generated-assets` under strict; there is no coverage for `plan-lint.sh`, `tests-touched.sh`, the dispatcher's unknown-check-name branch, the global `MODE=warn` strict→warn downgrade, the non-dispatcher back-compat path in `review-gate.sh:96-103`, or either new `doctor.py` helper — all of which carry the defects listed above.

The blanket `--repair` flag is now an ownership handoff: `maind.plan_provider_artifacts(repair=True)` passes every artifact ID, so any pre-existing unmanaged target that happens to match the render is silently adopted into the lock without the per-target preimage admission that the only other adoption path (`plan_exact_artifact_adoption`) and the D104/D108 bootstrap transfers require.

For `managed-blocks` artifacts tier 1 compares only the extracted-block hash, so a file whose surrounding unmanaged bytes are foreign is adopted as "byte-identical" and then rewritten whole by `_replacement_bytes` under `UPDATE`, which — unlike `REPAIR` — writes no `.provider-artifact.bak` pre-image.
Both new tests use the default `whole-file` boundary, leaving the `managed-blocks` adoption path (block-only match criterion, codec rewrite, absent backup) entirely unverified.

Symlink and dangling-symlink targets always yield `observed_hash is None` from `_managed_hash`, so they fall into tier 2 and receive advice ("diff against the render, then rerun with `--repair` once it matches") that can never succeed no matter what the operator does.

Every other `_classify` diagnostic is a stable kebab-token code consumed as such by harness/maind/tests, but tier 2 emits a variable multi-sentence prose message, breaking diagnostic-as-classification for downstream consumers.
The user-facing diagnostic advertises an owner `--adopt` decision/flag that exists nowhere in any CLI, and the test pins that substring, cementing a non-existent option in operator output.

Adoption semantics are now implemented twice (here and in `maind.plan_exact_artifact_adoption`) with divergent guards — the maind version refuses symlinks/non-regular files and demands an exact preimage set — against the monorepo rule that shared primitives live in one place in `core/`.

The changelog claims the tier-2 diagnostic names "класс расхождения" and a command, but the emitted message classifies nothing and contains no runnable command — only prose stating the content does not byte-match.
No test asserts projection/`plan_id` stability across differing roots for the new tier-2 diagnostic, which is exactly where the root-dependent absolute path enters the hashed identity.
